learning_outcomes.text: Know the fundamental principles of Thermodynamics and know how to apply them to perform global analyses of thermodynamic systems of engineering interest.
Perform laboratory setups, simulations, and experiments to verify theoretical results and acquire appropriate practical skills.
Understand and know how to use the thermodynamic relationships and diagrams that describe the different properties of substances.
Know and understand the fundamentals of psychrometry and its application to different industrial devices and processes.
Know the basic thermodynamic power and refrigeration cycles and their main engineering applications.
Know how to analyze energy processes and their efficiency.

syllabus_topics: 2.6. Isochoric and isobaric transformations. Enthalpy. Adiabatic transformations.
2.7. Applications to ideal gases: Joule's and Mayer's laws, internal energy and enthalpy of ideal gases.
3.9. Applications to ideal gases: Entropy of ideal gases.
3.11. The dependence between internal energy and volume
5.8. Internal energy, enthalpy, and entropy of a liquid+saturated vapor mixture
5.9. Property tables of a pure substance
6.5. Rankine cycle or basic ideal steam turbine cycle. Thermal efficiency of the Rankine cycle.
6.7. Refrigeration systems with compressor. Reverse cycle or Carnot refrigeration cycle. Vapor compression cycle.
7.3. Adiabatic mixing of two moist air streams
assessment_rules: The assessment is divided into two parts: Laboratory (LAB) and Theory and Problems (TyP). The final grade (NF) is calculated as 84% × TyP + 16% × LAB. To pass the course, a LAB score of at least 5 and a TyP score of at least 4 are required, with a final grade (NF) of 5 or higher (all scores out of 10). In the ordinary call, the highest score between the progressive and global evaluation options will be considered for each part (LAB and TyP). If the course is not passed, parts with a grade of 5 or higher can be retained for the extraordinary call; only the LAB grade (≥ 5) can be carried over to successive academic years.
